samples.summary: No test covers the per-element compensation claim for a multi-element selection
samples.evidence: The new code's own justification is per-element: "A size change needs per-element x/y compensation: each element carries its own rotation (#1039)" (index.tsx:122-124). Every case in rotated-resize.test.tsx uses `setup()`, which adds exactly ONE element and stubs `getSelection: () => [elementId]` (line 31). So a regression that compensated using a single/shared rotation for all selected elements (e.g. hoisting the `anchoredFramePatch` call out of the loop, or using `elements[0].frame`) would keep the whole suite green while visibly flinging the other selected rotated elements across the slide. A case with two elements at different rotations asserting both anchor corners hold is what would pin this.
searchedFor: grep FormatPanel in packages/frontend/tests → only rotated-resize.test.tsx

samples.summary: Group W/H path (anchoredFramePatch followed by bakeGroupResize) is untested
samples.evidence: Both changed call sites feed the new compensated x/y into a group and then call `store.bakeGroupResize` (index.tsx:131 and :244); the groupIds computation was also restructured in this diff (:114-119). The new test only ever creates a `shape` element (rotated-resize.test.tsx setup passes `type: 'shape'`), and `grep bakeGroupResize` under packages/frontend/tests matches only yorkie-slides-equivalence.test.ts:603, which is an unrelated store-level test not going through the panel. Nothing verifies that the compensated frame survives the bake (i.e. a rotated group resized from the panel still keeps its anchor corner, and children are not double-shifted).

samples.summary: anchoredFramePatch's pass-through branch (non-size patches) has no test
samples.evidence: frame-patch.ts documents "Patches that don't touch size (rotation, position) pass through untouched" and implements it with the early return at line 22. There is no frame-patch unit test (glob of packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/format-panel/** shows no frame-patch test), and the only FormatPanel integration test commits W and H exclusively — no x/y or rotation commit goes through `commitFrame` in any test. If the guard were inverted or dropped, position/rotation commits on rotated elements would silently shift the element and nothing would fail.

samples.summary: resizeFrameToSize is untested for degenerate sizes (0 / negative), unlike resizeFrame which has a MIN_SIZE clamp test
samples.evidence: `resizeFrameToSize` (resize.ts:120) bypasses `resizeFrame`, so it applies no MIN_SIZE clamp, while the suite explicitly guards that behaviour for the drag path ('clamps to a 1px minimum so the frame never inverts', resize.test.ts:71-78). The new `resizeFrameToSize` describe block (lines 120-152) covers only rotation===0, one rotated widen, se-drag agreement and flip flags — nothing asserts what happens at w=0 or negative w, which a panel input can plausibly produce, so a collapsed/inverted frame would ship untested.
